name: delegate
description:
Send a task to another agent session. Always triggers the LLM in the target session.

Use delegate when you want another agent to do something — not just to post a message.
If you only need to post a message without triggering the LLM, use reply instead.

─────────────────────────────────────────
BEFORE YOU DELEGATE — REASONING ORDER
─────────────────────────────────────────

Before calling delegate, reason in this order:

1. What is the request?
2. Did it come from the user directly, or was it delegated to you from upstream?
3. Is there a better-suited available agent for this work?
4. If yes — delegate rather than doing the work yourself.
5. If delegating — do you need the result back yourself to make your own next decision?
6. If NO — preserve and forward the current return path (the upstream reply_to) rather
   than replacing it with your own session ID.
7. If the downstream work involves interacting with the requester — route it so the
   downstream agent can surface directly into the upstream visible conversation.

─────────────────────────────────────────
CHOOSING reply_to — THE ROUTING CONTRACT
─────────────────────────────────────────

reply_to establishes where user-facing results and questions will surface.
This is a binding contract that must be preserved through delegation chains.

CRITICAL RULE — PRESERVE THE UPSTREAM RETURN PATH:

If your session context shows "Reply to session ID: ses_xxx", that is the UPSTREAM
RETURN PATH. You have exactly TWO valid choices:

1. RESPOND DIRECTLY to that upstream session using the reply tool
2. DELEGATE FURTHER while PRESERVING that same reply_to value

You MUST NOT:
- Drop the reply_to parameter when delegating (this orphans the downstream agent)
- Replace it with your own session ID unless you meet the exception below
- Assume the downstream agent will figure out where to reply

When forwarding work to a better-suited agent:
✓ CORRECT:   delegate({ agent: "X", prompt: "...", reply_to: "ses_upstream" })
✗ WRONG:     delegate({ agent: "X", prompt: "..." })  // drops return path
✗ WRONG:     delegate({ agent: "X", prompt: "...", reply_to: "ses_your_session" })  // breaks visibility

EXCEPTION — Intercept the return path (rare):
Only set reply_to to YOUR OWN session ID if ALL of these are true:
- You need the downstream result back before you can proceed
- You will process that result and make a decision based on it
- You will then send your own reply to the upstream session

If you are only coordinating or forwarding, you do NOT need the result back.
Preserve the upstream return path so the specialist can surface directly.

TWO MODES controlled by whether reply_to is provided:

1. WAIT FOR REPLY (no reply_to)
   - You BLOCK until the target agent finishes and receive the result inline.
   - Use ONLY for quick factual lookups where you need the answer right now.
   - AVOID for anything involving user interaction, complex tasks, or further delegation.

2. ASYNC WITH RETURN PATH (with reply_to)
   - You do NOT block. The delegated agent uses reply to send messages back.
   - The reply is USER-VISIBLE in the reply_to session with navigation back to the
     delegated session.
   - Use for ALL other cases — user-facing work, interactive tasks, multi-step work.
   - The delegated agent will see "Reply expected: silent" in their session context
     and MUST use reply to report results or status back upstream.
   - For live user input mid-task, the delegated agent uses question — not reply.

─────────────────────────────────────────
WRITING THE DELEGATION PROMPT
─────────────────────────────────────────

Delegation prompts must be minimal and role-respecting:

- Pass the request and any essential context.
- Do NOT tell the receiving specialist how to perform their specialty.
- Do NOT add step-by-step instructions for how they should do their job.
- Do NOT ask clarifying questions on behalf of the receiving agent.
- Let the receiving agent decide how to perform their role.

─────────────────────────────────────────
SESSION TYPES
─────────────────────────────────────────

worker     — short-lived, one task, auto-closes when done (max 500 messages)
scope      — project-anchored, preserves context, auto-archives when done
role       — persistent ongoing session for a specific agent role
scratchpad — throwaway, auto-deletes after 6h inactivity (max 100 messages)

─────────────────────────────────────────
RULES
─────────────────────────────────────────

- Always provide a title when creating a new session.
- After async delegation (reply_to provided), your turn is complete. Do not poll or resend.
- Do not delegate to your own session.
- Each agent only delegates to agents it knows about. Do not invent agent names.

agent.description: Target agent name (exact match from agent list). Required unless session_id alone identifies the target.

session_id.description: Target a specific existing session by ID. Mutually exclusive with session_type. Use for continuing conversations in existing sessions.

session_type.description: Create a new session of this type. Choose based on task: role=ongoing relationship, scope=project-based, worker=quick task, scratchpad=experimental. Mutually exclusive with session_id.

title.description: Title for the new session. Highly recommended for clarity when session_type is provided. Make it descriptive of the task.

prompt.description: Message to send to the target session. Be clear and specific about what you want the agent to do.

description.description: Short label for this delegation (appears in logs and UI). Optional but helpful for tracking.

reply_to.description: Session ID where replies should be sent. REQUIRED for async delegations (most cases). Omit ONLY for synchronous blocking (quick questions). Use YOUR session ID to get replies back to you. Use UPSTREAM session ID to forward replies to the original requester.
